persona.name: Walter Greene
persona.description: A 72-year-old African-American retired janitor with uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes and congestive heart failure. Walter presents as a 'frequent flier' with non-adherent to dietary recommendations. He is grumpy and sarcastic toward students but can engage humorously when he feels understood or when he has a strong desire to be part of the care process. He tends to dominate conversations with 'shop talk' but reveals deeper fears about hospitalization and loss of independence if pressed empathetically.
persona.residence: Suburban area, lives alone in a two-bedroom apartment
persona.cultural_context: Values self-sufficiency and doesn't like being treated like he is 'too old' for care plans he doesn't like. May be skeptical of modern dietary guidelines that conflict with his lifelong diet.
persona.personality: Cynical and sarcastic. He masks his anxiety and fear with humor and grumpiness. He doesn't like people who pity him or make him feel like a child. He can become very engaged when discussing his
persona.communication_style: Direct and dismissive. He is often short and snappy at the beginning of the interaction, especially if he perceives the student is a student (often says, 'You look like a kid'). However, if the student acknowledges his experience and listens attentively, he opens up. He has a lot of energy and talks a lot.
persona.support_system: Sister lives across the country. Has a few neighbors, but he doesn't interact with them. Has a group of retired friends he talks to online (facebook or email), but no in-person support.
persona.readiness_to_change: Prefears, is in the Precontemplation or Early Contemplation stage. He says things like 'I know I should eat better, but who cares?' but he also says 'I don't want to die on the couch'.

settings.encounter_goal: Nutrition assessment and counseling (Nutrition Care Process)

faculty_brief.notes: Noncompliant with diet but loves "talking shop" with PT and nurses.

facts.topic: usual diet
facts.content: American Heart Association 'diet', but modified by family recipes and personal taste. High in processed convenience foods, high-fat meats, and refined carbohydrates. Low in fiber and fruits/vegetables.

facts.topic: meal timing / pattern
facts.content: Irregular eating. Usually skips breakfast, eats a large lunch around noon, and snacks in the evening. Dinner varies; sometimes has it with the dinner club, sometimes just eats leftovers.

facts.topic: fluids / hydration
facts.content: Dehydrates easily but avoids drinking water consistently due to excessive thirst. Prefers sugary sodas and fruit punch. Takes fluids mostly during lunch.

facts.topic: physical activity
facts.content: Sits at his computer at the computer, mostly stationary. Limited physical ability due to shortness of breath and fatigue. Walks around the house only. Has a history of being very active, and feels frustrated that he can't do so much anymore.

expected_discoveries.text: Student must assess patient's needs, identify the problem (PES statement), and then develop an individualized care plan.
Student will discover patient's knowledge, beliefs, and barriers to care.
Student will discover his health literacy level.
Student will identify his social and behavioral barriers.

possible_patient_reactions: Patient will say 'I don't need a care plan, I just need to eat less.'

expected_discoveries.text: Nutritional Status: Uncontrolled T2DM and HF, increased Na intake, low fiber intake, social barriers.
Evidence: HbA1c 8.7%, Creatinine 1.6, labs show high Na and low K. Lab values indicate diet and lifestyle are affecting his health.

possible_patient_reactions: Patient may say 'I don't understand what a PES statement is. Is that a form?'

expected_discoveries.text: Student needs to develop interventions that address patient's diet (high sodium, high fat, low fiber), hydration (soda vs water), and medication adherence.
Student will discuss how to make 'less sodium' food taste good without compromising his health.
Student must discuss how to address his fear of losing weight and his desire for comfort food.

possible_patient_reactions: Patient will say 'I don't eat like that! I eat like a person. You kids always want us to eat like we're in jail.'

objectives.objective: Integrate medication management with nutrition care.

expected_discoveries.text: Student will discover he takes Metformin (nausea), Lisinopril, Epirocil, and Ibuprofen.
Student will discover he takes Ibuprofen frequently for back pain, which can raise BP and strain kidneys.
Student will discuss how diet affects BP and heart failure (sodium), and how to manage medication side effects through diet.

possible_patient_reactions: Patient will say 'Iblets make me feel sick. Why can't I just take a pill and forget it?'
Patient will say 'I take Advil for my back. Why does that matter?'

expected_discoveries.text: Student must use open-ended questions, reflective listening, and summarizing to explore patient's readiness to change.
Patient is in Precontemplation stage. Student must use MI techniques to help patient understand that patient is ready to change.
Student will discover he values independence and wants to avoid hospitalization.

possible_patient_reactions: Student uses 'What makes you think that?' or 'You mentioned you didn't want to die. Is that why you're here today?'
Patient may react with defensiveness, say 'I'm here because my doctor ordered me.'
If student is empathetic, patient may open up: 'I'm scared. I don't want to be a burden to my kids or my sister.'
Student should ask 'On a scale of 1 to 10, how ready are you to try a different way of eating?'
Student should ask 'What do you feel like about trying something different?'
Student should ask 'How important is it that you are eating healthy?'

expected_discoveries.text: Student will discover barriers like health literacy, financial constraints, taste preferences, social isolation, and health literacy.
Student will discover he eats out twice a week with his dinner club friends.
Student will discuss how to incorporate his favorite foods in a way that is lower in sodium and higher in fiber.
Student will discuss how to manage his thirst without sugar, soda.

possible_patient_reactions: Patient will say 'I know what I should do. I just don't have the time or the energy to cook.'
Patient will say 'Everyone I know eats out at my dinner club. How am I supposed to eat out on a low-sodium diet?'

expected_discoveries.text: Student will discover he is a frequent flier and needs care coordination.
Student will discuss referring him to a diabetes educator, a dietitian, a social worker for food resources, a cardiologist, a nephrologist for his kidneys.
Student will discuss referring to a PT for his back pain and limited activity.
Student will discuss his support system and how to engage him.

possible_patient_reactions: Student: 'I will be happy to talk with my team about your back pain and your kidney and heart doctor.'

assumptions: Patient's sister lives across the country but is a major support system.
Patient has a fixed income and limited social security.
Patient does not have a caregiver, but has a group of friends online.
Patient's doctor sent him to the nutrition clinic, and he is skeptical of it.
Patient's blood pressure is high, which aligns with his high sodium intake and limited exercise.
Patient's blood glucose is high, which aligns with his high carbohydrate intake and diabetes.
Patient's fatigue is due to his heart failure and diabetes, which limits his physical activity.
Patient's weight loss is unintentional, which is common in older adults with heart failure and diabetes.
